reviews.text: Full video review: https://youtu.be/esQ2M8Pnsd8 Carmageddon: Rogue Shift doesn’t have much in common with the old games, and some might be turned off by that, but it absolutely crushes it as a roguelite combat racer. Gameplay is addictive, the car list, weapons and upgrades allow for varied builds and strategies, and each run can be completed in around an hour, give or take. This is a shockingly good game, and this is coming from me, a guy who doesn’t typically play roguelites. Recommended to fans of games like Full Auto or Burnin Rubber.

Review with 4K screenshots and videos: https://www.pcmrace.com/2026/02/04/carmageddon-rogue-shift-review-pc/ With last year’s announcements of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Screamer reboot, and Carmageddon: Rogue Shift, 2026 seemed poised to be a great year for arcade racers—a genre that feels more missed than ever today. That’s why, when I learned that Italian studio 34BigThings had taken the reins of the Carmageddon franchise, my expectations rose immediately. Even considering that Redout and Redout 2 aren’t among my favorite anti-gravity racers—mainly due to their lack of weapons and almost exclusive focus on speed—the prospect of seeing Carmageddon reinvent itself with a more aggressive, modern approach sounded, at least on paper, very promising. Rogue Shift was announced as a single-player racing roguelite and, while it wasn’t what many were expecting, it didn’t strike me as a bad decision either. Especially when you consider that blending roguelite mechanics with other genres—like beat ’em ups (and I’m thinking of Absolum here)—has proven to be exactly what those genres needed to break out of their mold and offer far more substantial experiences. On top of that, there was a clearer emphasis on vehicular combat through mounted firearms, a new direction for Carmageddon, which has historically leaned more on physics, running over pedestrians, and chaos than on weaponry as a core system. With Carmageddon: Rogue Shift, 34BigThings promised gameplay that combined elements from classics like Burnout, Death Rally, Split/Second, Twisted Metal, and Vigilante 8, among others. The reality, however, is that this new entry in the series has little to none of what those games represent. Even focusing purely on handling, it doesn’t feel particularly arcade-like and can actually be exasperating in certain situations—such as when the car skids and flips over, forcing us to press the reset button, since getting back on track manually is awkward and unintuitive. The car feels far too glued to the ground and both sense of speed and drifting and are not satisfying at all. Something similar happens when crashing into track obstacles or into certain police vehicles that try to block us and end up getting “stuck” to our car like butter that’s hard to shake off. The recovery time is about as un-arcade as it gets, and this affects both the overall race dynamics and the game’s pacing, which ends up feeling inconsistent. To make matters worse, the AI drivers are, at best, accommodating, and the boss battles at the end of each segment offer little challenge if you play it safe. The problem isn’t that the game leans into chaos or aggression, but that it rarely manages to make that chaos feel fun or satisfying behind the wheel—something absolutely essential in any arcade racer. In more than one race, a single poorly timed crash can cost you several seconds with no real chance of recovery, knocking you out of contention long before the event ends and completely shattering the aggressive racing fantasy the game tries to sell. Adding to this ordeal is a track design that’s hard to justify and not very fun to navigate, with overly narrow sections, sudden sharp turns cluttered with pillars, and the occasional platform that serves as an alternate route. Since the AI sometimes falls behind due to its slowness or because of the presence of tougher or more peculiar Wasted (zombies) that explode or slow cars down, it doesn’t take long before enemy vehicles start attacking us even while driving the wrong way. Honestly, I’m not sure whether this is the result of a design flaw or AI issues—which wouldn’t surprise me—or simply intentional cruelty on the developers’ part. If there’s one aspect of Carmageddon: Rogue Shift that stands out positively, it’s the soundtrack. It features several fairly solid tracks that fit well with the franchise’s theme, mostly heavy metal (and even thrash metal) compositions loaded with guitar riffs and double bass, trying to fill the audio void left by the rest of the game. It’s a shame the developers didn’t lean into Carmageddon’s classic sensationalism by including a commentator who could at least call out checkpoints (as in Max Damage) or add some spice during crashes and eliminations, which on their own lack impact and excitement. The roguelite mechanics themselves aren’t poorly implemented. At the end of each run—successful or not—we earn Beatcoins, which can then be used to unlock new passives, perks, cars, weapons, and other elements. The issue is that this is a car game where no vehicle can be mechanically upgraded beyond these passive and active bonuses, which leaves a bitter aftertaste. As with any roguelite, during runs you can modify or upgrade your car’s loadout and weapons, repair it, and even take part in a kind of lottery that can grant various items. The races themselves are divided into death races (the most common mode), survival events, and elite events. In some branches of progression, we can choose which type of event to take on, allowing us to earn more points for that run or more Beatcoins. Given how forgiving the AI is, I didn’t run into major issues even in the tougher events. The only real challenge comes in elite events, where finishing in first place is mandatory, while in survival events you need to endure for two laps and reach the finish in time. In the remaining events, placing among the top three is enough to advance to the next round. Setting content aside, the visual presentation of Carmageddon: Rogue Shift doesn’t differ much from other recent combat racers. In fact, if it had a different name and didn’t include zombies—used to charge your boost—I probably wouldn’t notice many differences. The illustrations shown during the tutorial and before facing the three bosses are quite decent, but that same art style never really carries over into the races themselves. Despite using Unreal Engine 5, the graphical fidelity is far from impressive. The game features a very poor lighting system, where at times the screen can go completely black, with overly harsh lights and abrupt transitions that do nothing to help the overall experience. By editing the GameUserSettings.ini file and tweaking some options from 3 to 4, I noticed an increase in visual fidelity, but it came with frequent FPS drops and very unstable overall performance. Optimization doesn’t help matters either, especially considering that Carmageddon: Rogue Shift isn’t exactly a visually demanding title. Hardware ray tracing seems to add virtually nothing—reflections are practically nonexistent—so I’d recommend leaving it off. With a Ryzen 7 9850X3D and a GeForce RTX 5070 Ti at 4K, using the Epic preset without DLSS, I could barely maintain 60 FPS, when this setup should easily be pushing well over 100 FPS. There isn’t much more to add: Carmageddon: Rogue Shift ends up being a missed opportunity. While the idea of combining arcade racing with roguelite mechanics isn’t bad on paper, and the soundtrack does just enough to maintain the franchise’s identity, the final result falls well short of expectations. Unsatisfying handling, frustrating track design, inconsistent AI, and a weak technical presentation turn the experience into a slog more often than it should be. It’s not a completely irredeemable game, and there are interesting ideas that work within the genre’s boundaries, such as some event variety and a progression system that does its job. However, these positives aren’t enough to make up for a gameplay foundation that never truly comes together, nor to justify the return of such an iconic franchise under this interpretation. The result is an uneven experience, with a few redeeming moments, but one that fails to sustain interest or enjoyment in any consistent way. Carmageddon: Rogue Shift is a comeback that promised chaos and fun, but ultimately delivers more punishment than reward.

Ok, after 3 hours of playtime. I can say that I do recommend it. However, this is not going to be for everyone, and its price is eye watering, given what it contains and restrains....but hear me out. When I jumped in I was disappointed, none of the original characters, no customisation and no multiplayer or splitscreen...but then I dug deeper. When you load in, you might be disappointed by the lack of options, but the gameplay delivers exactly what is promised. Power ups, environmental kills and AI that can really mess up your chances to get first place. Not to mention the weapons that each vehicle is equipped with. Machine guns, rocket launchers, saw off shotguns, lasers, railguns and more. The only way to win is to fight dirty, but you slip up, mistime, or even get cocky...kiss your chances goodbye. You might walk away with a few wins as you rise up the ranks, but that leads to the next race where your cars damage remains into the next track. Think of it as a Wreck fest fever dream with someone blaring heavy metal music in your ear during a Mad Max marathon. As you progress through the races you notice that the AI and even the tracks become harder to navigate, even though you have been getting your 1st, 2nd and 3rd places...these all lead you to the main antagonists on the manslaughterfield, the bosses. Each one is determined to ruin your day with explosives, flamethrowers and a dirty side swiping mind...just the way it should be. You have a certain amount of time to take him out before it takes you out. You'll drift, shoot, explode and pick everything you can alive...but then the timer reaches zero and GAME OVER! WHAT?! THATS BULLS***! Ok ill just respond and NOPE! This is a Roguelite Arcade Vehicular Combat Game. Everytime you die, no matter where you are, you restart from the start...but with all the knowledge and credits to chsnge the outcome. Even better than that though there might be a not as many levels as you think they would have it is only randomly generated and each layout has been changed so it never feels like the same races. But better than that is where its concept of customising comes in. Using bitcoins (no not that bitcoin) you have the ability to purchase new upgrades in the shop, new weapons, new armor variants, new power ups, and even new cars for a different way to play. Maybe the heavier truck isnt your speed...how about a wildcard that randomly changes the cars abilities each time a new race starts. The possibilities are endless. I am on my 7th playthrough and I still haven't beaten it! That should shoe you replayablity, you will spend hours trying to unlock and find the best combination that works for you. And when you hit that accelerator you feel like a God of Destruction! Zombies get you more points to upgrade and csn be used to slow your opponents down as well environmental kills and distractions, but if you arent lucky you could be caught in the crossfire. But trust when I say, that when that 10 second timer begins to tick down and you have to think on your feet about getting that repair kit, with an onslaught of enemies behind you, rockets and bullets flying...you hit that repair point and it fixes about 10% of your car...you feel that same adrenaline rush everytime. Side note: its price is hard to swallow. At 50 USD (70 AUD) it is a lot to pay for something that feels like its more in the $25 range. So my only suggestion, wait till it goes on sale. 34 big things did an amazing job and doesnt feel like a shell of a Product, there is genuine care, honor and fun in it, but that price...is not a good way to show it. This isn't the Carmegeddon we know and grew up with. This isn't about getting to the finish, detroying all opponents or even killing all pedestrians...its more than that. Its a faster paced, adrenaline shredding, vehicllular combat arcade racer that forces your foot on the gas and wont stop till you are a splatter on the pavement. Then reload and do it again! I said to myself, oh this is garbage and will be returning it before the 2 hours...but 30 mins in...I felt this level of love I haven't felt since the Twisted Metal and Burnout days with splashes of Blur mixed in. If you are looking for a Carmegeddon game like the original, pick up Max Damage...but if you are willing to try a new era of car combat, with pure metal on metal, blood soaked viscera then look no further! This is one ride you will never forget.

This game is not like your regular Carmageddon (I grew up playing a lot of 2), so if you're expecting anything like the older carmageddons, get Max Damage. This is why the game has mostly negative reviews. This is Carmageddon, but strictly a racing game. There is no option to wreck all enemies to win, there is no option to kill all peds to win. However, had they just replicated the original (Which they already did), it would also be review bombed for being rehashed. Let's set aside the Carmageddon name. You have a very fun vehicular combat game. Race laps, destroy enemies with your weapons/car. Its a pretty simple gameplay loop, very hard to mess up. The big thing that really sets this game apart is that it is now a Roguelike. You upgrade your car, your weapons, and perks to help you get an edge in battle. This is what really interested me. I am not a fan of roguelikes, but I am a fan of racing games, and I think how they approached this was the best way to breathe life into the franchise. What you see is what you get, but what you get is a pretty damn solid game. The good, the graphics look very solid, it is a nice pick up and play game (You can also quit out of the tournament and return back if you'd like). Vehicular combat sounds are great. Ran just fine on my PC. The game does have some degree of rubberbanding, but I think its done quite well. The path you take on your journey will also rotate so you arent just driving the same tracks from the start. The bad, Soundtrack unfortunately is a bit generic. The car and track choice could use a few more cars and a bit more character so no Ski resorts beaches or the like. You're stuck with a war torn apocalypse. The characters kind of take a back seat to the action, so while they are in here, its just in name only (So far). The handling can use a tiny bit of work. There are zombies instead of peds. I also have absolutely no idea why on God's Green Earth the starter Mustang is FWD. TL;DR Don't listen to everyone upset that its not like the old Carmageddon. This game is fun. What you see is what you get but its a damn fun time. Wait for a sale though

Tl,dr: Game's good, not Carmageddon by any stretch, solid game direction, little variety for events/bosses. It's as if the developers went inside my brain, looked around every nook and cranny, then said "ok, let's make THIS game". I could only dream for a car-battler roguelike like this as a kid. Carmageddon Rogue Shift is not Carmageddon, it's true, I don't know who has to take the blame, but after so much time since the last Carmageddon, I understand the OG fans being angry about it, please take the game for itself, not as an IP holder. Most of the negative reviews are people review bombing for this reason. It's too early to tell how good the replayability will be, but after the first run, there were already upgrades that unlocked more playstyles. The handling requires time to get used to, but I can see how some people may not like it right off the bat. Try lowering steering sensitivity a bit. After having played it more, the bones for a strong racing game/battler are there, but there is just too little variety to justify the full price tag right now. While you have a decent choice with builds and cars, the main issue are the events, which are just race, race but FIRST, and race but more carefull for zombies. At least a couple modes more to take advantage of the game itself like roadrage or somekind of deathmatch in an arena would help a lot. Also, some areas are too dark, you can barely see what's infront, while that may be by design, it still feels too much. The first stage is the weakest, with no upgrades or weird powerups, but every run gest way better after that. The last boss is by far the coolest, but unless I did something wrong, it seemed off: the best way to tackle it was to brake, sit back, and shoot long range weapons, might get patched. The game truly is something special, but there's still potential unexplored, hopefully a major patch or dlc in the future helps expanding it. A 70% to 80% positive rating would be much closer to the quality of the game right now. #FRATELLIII D'ITALIIAAAA#

It's important to understand that this is very much a roguelite. You do runs consisting of branching path races with boss battles after a certain number of races, and there are upgradable components (guns, speed, etc.) during the runs and also permanent upgrades done outside of runs. Because of this, your car stinks at first. Slow, sludgy, and weak. This is the gamble they took in this game by making a [i]driving game[/i] a roguelite and handing you a doodoo car at the start. Each new car you unlock is a little better at something or other, but I suggest you make a beeline to unlock the SQR-NE55, which I think is a level 4 or 5 car (out of 10?). THAT car handles exactly like you're expecting cars to handle in a non-roguelite racing game. I beat the game with it, also placing 1st in every race along the way. The game goes from WTF hard to almost a little too easy once you upgrade. But that's a roguelite. The boss battles are a lot of fun. I think there are three rotating ones and my favorite is instead of a race it's you vs. a big 'ol boss truck, his half-sized main side kick, and a bunch of little protector cars, running however many laps you need in 5 minutes until you destroy him. Or you can destroy everyone, but you need to destroy the big guy in 5. The end boss battle is cool too but I'm not going to spoil it. Holding down on D-pad to respawn is key once or twice a race. Since this is primarily a car combat game and everyone is firing at you along with there being a lot of obstacles in the road, you're going to spin out a fair amount and it takes forever to make a multi-point turn to drive forward again. Just respawn. Having beaten the game I'd really like to see some other modes now, like to be able to choose the track, race type, and amount of enemies. Or maybe a daily challenge with leaderboards, some reason to want to come back and play it more often. The game is pretty good, maybe not worth the price right now if you're not an arcade racer junkie like myself, but with some post-launch refinements to the gameplay this could end up being a nice one. I'd bet money they're going to make the starting car better, because apparently people can see things like "roguelite" and a mile long list of car upgrades and still think the driving is just bad while being oblivious to what type of game they're playing.

But it's a damn fun one. I'd say I'm a huge fan of the series, the thrill of driving head first into a huge JCB type thing and killing it in one blow, the little chuckle every time I got knocked off my podium by a champagne bottle, being able to kill all the pedestrians and win the race despite doing nothing. Yeah I miss that. But this game brings so much other good stuff. Yes, it has it's performance problems, the handling of the car isn't amazing but I LOVE roguelite/roguelike games and this for me might just be the best one. The price is expensive, but I feel with the content already in the game and potential of what's to come I'd rather pay £36 for this than £60-70 for a AAA game that's mediocre. I just see the price in comparison to the current "how much games cost" fiasco. All in all, the reviews that say it's not Carmageddon are right but also did I want to play old Carmageddon and have the opportunity to strap a laser beam to my car and go round melting holes in my enemies. I did. Now I can. :)

As a longtime fan of the Carmageddon series, I have a message for the skeptics: judge the game for what it actually is, rather than what it isn't. There’s a vocal group of purists acting as if this title personally came over and thrashed their nostalgic memories of a niche franchise that once grabbed headlines 30 years ago. The reality is that this isn't a direct sequel, a reboot, or a replacement for the classic titles—and it never claimed to be. It’s a spin-off. And a damn good one, too. Once you stop punishing the developers for changing the formula, you find a fantastic car-combat game that successfully blends the brand's DNA with fresh mechanics for the racing genre. I love the original games, but let’s be honest: their appeal is an acquired taste. While the racing was straightforward, the "destroy all racers" and [i]especially[/i] "kill all pedestrians" win conditions could become a tedious slog. I'm sorry, but that is the honest truth. The series has a flow problem. That's why this title cuts that fat to keep the high-octane carnage constant. While the open-ended maps are gone, they’ve been replaced by well-crafted linear circuits. These tracks feel distinctly "Carmageddon," taking you through: [list] [*]Ruined city streets and storm drain systems [*]Through buildings! [*]Half-sunken cargo ships and power plants [*]Plane graveyards and winding forest roads [*]and that's just a few because I've been dying before the 3rd boss... [/list] The Sidebash—which I call the "f**k you button"—is first permanent upgrade the game forces you to equip. And it is [i]incredibly[/i] satisfying. The collisions feel heavy and visceral. Just like the classics, there is no "player advantage" here; the AI and police are just as dangerous to themselves as they are to you. You’ll see the same glorious buffoonery as opponents slam each other into walls, go flying off sidewalls, and they can spin you out just as easily as you can them. And speaking of dangers, the inclusion of zombies isn't just a "safe" play to avoid the censorship that plagued the series. Here, they serve a mechanical purpose. Different variants act as tactical tools and hazards to avoid: [list] [*]Boomer Zombies: Puss zombies that explode and do massive damage. [*]Mortar Plants (Idk if that's their actual name): Giant fauna that litter the map with bombs. [*]Siren: A crazy, indescribable anomaly that stuns drivers. [*]Residuum: Leftovers of organic matter from the zombies such as droppable pods, sticky stops, pod bombs, etc. [*]if there is more, I haven't seen it but I haven't gotten that far in my current runs. [/list] While weapons provide an assist, your best tool remains the impact. The new dedicated slam button (which doubles as an evade) removes the frustration of having to line up the "perfect" assault, keeping the flow of combat fast. Each weapon type has their utility but your choices in perks and loadouts is what can make or break a run. Your top priority is build synergy; making sure your perks and your loadout compliment each other perfectly. The loop is tight and follows a classic roguelite structure: [b]Proceduralization:[/b] Events, reward, reward conditions, and tracks are fully randomized. [b]Select:[/b] Pick a car with a preset build. [b]Compete:[/b] Complete events to earn currency for perks, upgrades and weapons. [b]Progress:[/b] Fight bosses and tackle endurance rounds to reach the next sector, earning you bonus slots to add more perks and upgrades upping the ante. [b]Strategy:[/b] Picking a route best suits your goals. For example: Do you take on lower pay or riskier runs for a chance at a loot drop that has a 1 in 6 chance of taking anyway anything you earned, or do you prioritize maxing income before the next upgrade shop? [b]Die/Reset:[/b] Use your earnings to unlock better gear, starting perks, new shop items and vehicles for the next run. This game isn't Carmageddon in the traditional sense, but that doesn't make it not Carmageddon. It has the feel, the sound, the look, the grit, the music with newfound non-stop action and a roguelite foundation (which is practically alien to racing games as a genre). My only genuine complaint is the handling. The cars are too twitchy at low speeds and lose responsiveness at high speeds. It feels less like natural momentum and more like a "switch" in the code that kills your turning radius once you hit a certain MPH. However, if you can get past the handling quirks, you’ll find a great combat racer that wears its branding on its sleeve. So, after 21 years on Steam, this is my first-ever review, and also the first game I've ever asked for a refund on. Honestly, I really wanted to like this game. I didn't care about the series it came from, so I went in with no expectations. The 36 Euro price felt high right away, but I love Redout 2, so I wanted to support the folks who made it. I'll keep this short because who reads long reviews, right? What I Liked: - The idea behind the game is super cool – the trailers made me want to play it instantly. . The cars look awesome, like something out of Mad Max. - The tracks feel gritty and dangerous, which is a nice touch. - Some of the guns feel really powerful when you shoot other cars. What I Didn't Like (and why I refunded it): - Feels Cheap: Everything about it just feels low-budget, like it should cost way less than it does. - Bad Performance: The graphics look old (think PS3/PS4), and it runs terribly. Plus, some settings keep resetting (Xess to AMD FSR), which is annoying. - Annoying Bugs: I had a bug where the game told me I was going the wrong way after a simple turn. Also, when time runs out, you just explode without warning. - Too Easy Upgrades: You get way too many upgrade points. After just an hour and a half, I'd unlocked a third of everything, and I was just blindly upgrading stuff because I could do so many at once. - Repetitive & Boring: The music is super dull – just the same metal riffs over and over. And the tracks? They repeat constantly, making it feel like you've seen everything after one run. - Terrible Steering: This is the worst part. The cars oversteer like crazy, and there's a weird delay in controls. It just feels like you're never truly in charge of your car. How to Fix It? Simple: Fix all the bugs, drop the price a lot, add way more tracks, and please, please, add multiplayer! I may buy this again at a cheaper price, wait for some updates and review this again. Developers are allowed to redeem themselves and deserve a better review when doing so.

Oh boy, Carmageddon: Rogue Shift… more like Carmageddon: Wrong Shift. This thing has about as much to do with Carmageddon as a yoga retreat has to do with a monster truck rally. They slapped the name on it, but the soul, the chaos, the glorious vehicular carnage? Gone. It’s like they took Carmageddon, put it in a blender, hit “purée,” and poured out a generic indie driving gun game smoothie. Not even TDR 2000, the awkward cousin everyone pretends not to know, sinks this low. At least that one still had the DNA of Carmageddon buried under the jank. Rogue Shift? It’s like someone found the brand name in a bargain bin and thought, “Eh, let’s make a game about… racing around? add guns? Rouge like? Who cares!” If you want actual Carmageddon, do yourself a favor: fire up Max Damage, slap on the overhaul mod, and bask in the glorious symphony of twisted steel and screaming pedestrians. That’s Carmageddon. This? This is Carma‑geddon’t.

To start off, this is NOT a Carmageddon game. This is a bland, generic rogue-lite combat racer. This has none of the soul that made past Carmageddon games good. I can understand that this being a rogue-lite combat racer meant that it would lose a lot of what made the older games good. But this game is only a Carmageddon game in name only. The maps are too small and bland. Each Race has only one objective "finish the race", "Survive 2 laps", or "Defeat Boss" The cars all feel too similar and that the stats don't matter. Each car starts with a different weapon, but you can change these during a race if you wanted to mix and match Car and Weapon. The more i play this game, the more i find myself wanting to avoid races and just get to the end as quickly as possible and the less i actually enjoyed the game. Things I would love to see added in as either a patch, DLC, or a sequel. Larger maps for bigger races and better environments. Go over the top with this like the older games did. Have maps where you race on the rooftops of skyscrapers, on and in a massive air craft carrier. Give checkpoints, but allow people to explore and find their own way to the checkpoints. Better objectives. how about "Elimination: each racer has 3 lives. just be the last one alive" "extermination: kill 100 zombies" Bring back the classic Cars. Even the ones that don't make any logical sense! Personally, i would get a huge kick out of playing the giant spiked metal hamster ball from Carmageddon 3 again. Or the pickup truck with a giant drill on the front. If you're interested in a generic Combat Racer Rogue-Lite, then you may like this. But wait for it to go on sale. For everyone else... Don't bother with this. It has no connections at all to what made Carmageddon good and just really isn't that fun of a game.

You've seen the "THIS ISN'T CARMAGEDDON" reviews but, are you wondering if the game is just good? Don't care if it is or isn't Carmageddon? Well, its not, unfortunately. Here are some key points. - [b]The handling model is atrocious.[/b] I say this as a long time veteran of driving games, both arcade and sim. Low handling cars wheels turn so comically slowly you'll barrel straight into walls- no chicanes or s-curves for you, just wall. High handling cars are almost drivable- almost. - [b]There is virtually zero depth to the gameplay loop.[/b] 8 runs in and they've all felt nearly the same. The same tracks, the same bosses, where you employ the same tactics. Nothing mixes up a run, not even changing your car. You die, you start over, it feels exactly the same. - [b]The game is artificially difficult and you can't do much about it.[/b] You'll lose runs because the guy behind you is just pelting you with lazers or bullets; your only avenue to avoid this is to just slam on the brakes and let him pass you, which is a bit silly for a racing game, no? Not to mention the random zombie obstacles or rubberbanding opponents that can end your run on a whim. - The final boss is a giant worm that frankly isn't even that difficult to battle, but there is an [b]arbitrary time limit and if you take too long you just blow up.[/b] If you didn't level your weapon up enough to pass the DPS check, you just lose the entire run. Sorry! - The depth of content is [b]not worth $40[/b]. Maybe $20, maybe $30 on a good day and they clean up some of the problems I have with the game. There is no plot of any kind, every run feels the same, the progression between runs is shallow; the game gives you very little motivation to work toward anything other than the next +10% HP buff or a perk that lets you shoot your gun 10% faster or something. I wish I had some nice things to say about the game. It certainly [i]looks[/i] high effort, until you're holding the controller and playing it yourself.

[h1]开赛车+碾丧尸+肉鸽，这么有搞头的吗？[/h1] 本作是一款至少在玩法上相当有创意的游戏。玩家可以在荒芜的废土末世中按照自己想要的路线方式驱车前行，在与对手竞速、Battle的同时还可以在沿路无情的碾压行走的丧尸。游戏的画面虽然谈不上有多精细，但是有着多条环境迥异的赛道，可以保持相当时间的新鲜感。由于带有肉鸽元素，局外成长机制自然必不可少，玩家可以在黑市升级载具性能，配置各种武器。不过本作目前车辆整体的驾驶手感一般，属于娱乐向而非拟真向的类型。 [h1]你就这么飞驰人生？[/h1] 市面上赛车游戏很多、打丧尸游戏也不少，但是像这种直接在标准赛道上风驰电掣撞飞丧尸的还真不多见。理论上丧尸虽然聚集起来也能对你造成威胁（尤其是停车的时候），但是大部分时候可以通过车辆的高速奔驰将其撞飞。说实话，这种毫无负担不犯法的胡乱撞一片，还是挺解压的。 虽然丧尸并非最大的不安因素，但是你依然需要在各个赛道上打败对手。本作在赛道的推进流程上类似于爬塔游戏，玩家可以自主选择路线前行。通常来说，每个赛道都有一个主要目标和次要目标，前者通常是“进入XX名位次”，而后者则是“对敌人造成XX伤害、摧毁XX个敌人”等等。没错，除了氮气加速以及撞丧尸外，本作还可以利用车载武器去攻击敌人，颇有种战斗赛车的意味了。只不过弹药比较稀缺，需要在赛道上及时补充，也可以通过局外成长永久提升弹药补充效率。 作为飞驰人生的赛车，本作也提供了十余种赛车，每款赛车都有着操控、加速、最高速度以及攻击力等属性，且有着独特的预装武器和特技，还能通过比赛获得的毙车币进行全方位的升级。玩家可以根据每条赛道的特点合理配置出战赛车以及武器。不过从个人体验上来说，由于本作的转向操控着实有点糟心，非常不推荐那种厚重不灵活的车辆，否则就等着疯狂撞柱子吧。 [h1]总结[/h1] 总的来说，本作虽然驾驶手感比较一般，但是游戏的形式还是非常新颖的，感兴趣的倒也是可以体验一番。推荐使用手柄游玩，SD也亲测可玩。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

Cool concept - Poorly executed. I want to love this game. I've been a Carmageddon fan since the Dos era, and this just isn't it. - They've updated the handling since release, however many cars still over-steer and spin out with seemingly no way to prevent it. Take a hairpin corner, spin out, take a 90 degree corner, spin out, drive on a heavily banked area of track, spin out. No amount of braking, feathering the gas, or trying to drift seems to make a difference. Drifting almost immediately becomes a 180° spin. - The AI has rubber banding akin to Mario Kart, this becomes problematic with the aforementioned poor handling, in addition to this game being a 'roguelite' where failing one race, without a costly consumeable, means the end of your run. - The AI is not affected by race conditions, such as having to dispatch a boss, only having one life, etc, meaning they get to keep respawning, launching ordinance at you and spinning you out, while you are required to finish in 1st place (for some races) with only one life. Attempts to spin out the AI are pointless (unless you use your specific side-boost ability), as they seem to be stuck to their specific racing line. This becomes further problematic with the aforementioned poor handling and 'roguelite' structure. - Boost is gained by hitting 'peds'/'infected', this becomes an issue when you are spun out by the AI, have to reset to last place, only to find all the infected that would give you boost have already been run down by the group of AI that just spun you out. As a result, acceleration without boosting is actually quite slow, leaving you stuck at the back of the pack until you can eventually find more infected to finally build boost. - *Spoiler* The final boss - *Spoiler* The final boss is a timed battle/race against a giant sand worm with a giant health bar. If you do not kit your car out in a specific build, you will not be able to complete the race in the allotted time, as your weapons will just not do enough damage. Weapons, with the exception of a few, are auto-lock, meaning in many races, including boss battles, your weapon will lock on (and in some cases, auto-fire) at various targets during the race, such as environmental destructibles, other racers, or the boss. This becomes an issue when you are specifically trying to lock on to a boss, but your weapons keep locking on to, or auto-firing at, everything but the actual boss. Add all the other aforementioned issues with a final boss that has lock on points on its side, and it just leads to an overall frustrating experience. I want to love it and I appreciate the 'roguelite' experiment, but the poor handling and weird design decisions just kill the fun for me. Edit: "Big Update" today... The arena mode is a cool addition, except for the issue thay the car handling is still ♥♥♥♥. Also, you can only do any meaningful damage if you boost or "shunt" an opponent, this means you'll be trying to boost shunt your way around a demolition derby arena (in classic mode without weapon pickups). Unfortunately, the police also join this arena and smash the ♥♥♥♥ out of your car. This is once again problematic in the roguelite structure, because you can't do any meaningful damage without boosting (which you obtain by damaging opponents/peds). JetAss boss fight is still just ass. Controls seem to have gotten worse again. New Mitsubishi-like car spins out way too easy (shouldn't it be all wheel drive??). Honestly, ♥♥♥♥ this game at this point.

The reviews for this game from Carmageddon oldheads are so salty and hyperbolic that I had to try the game myself because the reviews can't be trusted. There's def a cool game here, but I have to agree it feels like there should be more. That said, $40 games like this tend to get regular updates, so I hope there's a lot more to come. There was a lot of complaining by the community about the vehicle handling early on, right now though the 4 vehicles I used handled pretty well. They do handle a bit differently from each other, like the small truck can start drifting just by turning harder instead of needing to tap the handbrake, while one of the lighter cars has way more grippy tires so it's harder to drift it. I think the tracks are well-designed, I can tell what's going on and can react in time to upcoming threats. For accessibility, there's even an option to slow the game speed down if you want. The tracks present different challenges and offer a chance to use different strategies. For example, one has a lot of small side lanes you can use to basically trap an opponent directly in front of you to light-up with a weapon with impunity. There's one with several big pipes you can drive through and use as ramps to get airtime and earn currency. There's one that's a big circle and littered with obstacles, the circular nature of the track makes it really hard to see what's coming up so you need to have good reflexes or memorize the position of the major obstacles. Clearly, what helps set this game apart from other racers are the zombies infesting the tracks. The basic zombies can present a threat and some opportunities for tactical play. Like you can bait exploding zombies to hit opponents, and you can try to sideram and stall an opponent in a mob of zombies so they get ravaged by the mob. There are giant leech-like Spitter zombies that lob loogies indiscriminately onto the track. There are more types I'm looking forward to discovering. There are vehicles that enter play other than the other racers, like "Enforcers" in police cars that try to wreck anyone. In one race I saw what looked like a special delivery van enter the field, but I couldn't figure out what it was for before all the savage action wrecked it lol. At certain checkpoints in your run, there are Boss vehicles that need to be wrecked. Don't feel bad if you don't beat them for a few runs, the point of the game is to get upgrades to make your car faster/stronger to be able to beat them. On top of that they require some strategy to beat, that may vary depending on what weapon you're using. Like if you're using a Machine Gun, you may want to sideram more often instead, to avoid exploding barrels being constantly dropped behind one of the Boss vehicles. And there seems to be variety, one of the Bosses you encounter can be beat by straight up racing better than them, instead of killing them. The weapons are familiar, Machine Gun, Shotgun, Missile Luncher, etc. A bit boring, but I like that there are variants, like the Launcher can be manually aimed to do more damage, instead of auto-aiming for less damage. There's a wiggly laser weapon I took a shine to. Your car can be equipped with perks (like more damage the longer you hold a weapon's trigger), you can swap/buy different ones in shops along your roadmap. There are synergies here and there, though the bonuses are pedestrian, like +10% Damage Reduction if you have 2 Armor Perks equipped at once or whatever. I like the game, though there are some significant bugs to watchout for: -One time the car hit a small object in the road that sent the car cartwheeling very high into the air, obviously unintended. It's like the kind of bug you'd see while driving in the Helldivers 2 FRV, where hitting a little rock will send you flying into orbit. -Another time, after landing from a jump, the car abruptly came to a complete stop, as if it had crashed into something, like maybe there as a stray hitbox/barrier there. -Several times I couldn't buy a Golden Ticket (let's you prevent losing once, or skip an event on your roadmap) in the Shop even though I had enough currency. The game doesn't support PS5 controllers, you have to use Steam Input, maybe that's causing an issue somehow. The issue keeps happening. -I finally survived the BS bugs and made it to the final boss, I start kicking the boss's butt, and the game doesn't like it so it throws a FATAL ERROR! Tl;dr review - it's a fun 20 - 30$ driving combat game for one or two play attempts in a session. Not something you'll be doing for a long run, but definitely worth a try. However, the game lacks certain adjustments and polish that hold it back from being a full recommend. Full review - This game gets to about 80% of its full potential. And yeah, a B-minus isn't a "bad" grade, but you definitely know it could do better. It sounds almost nitpicky to say that the game gets every concept about 80% right and that makes it frustrating, but when you PLAY it, and if you play other driving games, you feel why that last 20% can feel so bad. Let's just preview this with the starting menu loop. You select "new game" -> you go to the store -> You select a difficulty -> You select a car - > You start your run. Now here's the first rub: You can NOT break that cycle. If you're at the store and you want to exit out of the game? You have to go all the way to CAR SELECTION, then hit back and it takes you to the main menu. Oh but what if you're at car select and you want to change difficulty? Hit BACK to go to the MAIN MENU, and then go through the store and THEN you can change your difficulty. I present this not because that is the most unforgiveable sin a game menu has ever committed, but to put out the mindset of the game going forward. It's full of little things that someone probably pointed out, but was just not important enough to fix, no matter how small. Okay let's talk driving - I LOVE the weight and feel of the weapons aside from the laser gun. Heavy, chunky noises and effects and things go boom. Zombies are fun to drive through. Most impacts are satisfying, weighty moves that punish both parties and just has good game feel. The drifting on the other hand? And grip level in general? Well it's neither mario kart nor is it Forza Horizon, that much is for sure. And it's not so much about the grip level as it is when you have and don't have grip. Drifting is slow in this game - no boosts initially, but if you do it right you do gain boost for later. But you can easily find yourself spinning out without no real warning from the car, particularly if it has low grip to begin with. but then to get going again, its easy to powerslide in a loop and lose a ton of time. Meanwhile, the game's rubberbanding takes a lot of the thrill and edge off of all of this. If you're way into the lead, don't bother trying to extend it. THe enemies are getting free boost/speed and will be on your tail shortly. Or if you've got at least a lap left in the race, don't despair when you're dead last - you'll be back in the fight in just a few turns. So while it's hard to quantify the technical side of driving, I'm settling on the word "pointless". Which is a slight problem because you NEED to get a good result to keep your run going in most maps. But just have some faith that the game will provide and make sure you pick up weapon upgrades when you can and you'll be fine in the races themselves. I do wish the cars had a bit more momentum against the environment though, and the drift physics really do need some extra work. I get this isn't ridge racer, but a little bit of speed boost would go a long way towards making slipperier cars feel more satisfying. I think I'll end off by commenting on the overall gameplay loop - I think the economy is well balanced, you often have just enough to get the upgrades and weapons you need to succeed, but the game sometimes doesn't provide what your build needs in the shops, so some boss fights or races can become a slog. But that just happens sometimes in Rogue-likes. It's a hard game to play for multiple runs at a time though. The aforementioned fail due to bad luck in the shops is bad enough (this game has time limits for boss fights/races so unlike FTL or many other rogue-likes, you can't just have a slow fight and tough it out if you've got the HP) but having a great run hit the end stretch only to die in 15 seconds on a race because the guy behind you got a machine gun that murked you before you could even blink is VERY frustrating as it feels like the game has no counterplay or....no, I change my mind there - the game PUNISHES you for starting off too well. THe rubberbanding means enemies are always behind you and your weapons can't shoot back. You WILL lose a run or two to an enemy behind just mowing you down on the first lap because you rushed into the lead. Or you lose a run after leading a race the entire time only to spin out because you drifted too hard on the final turn, and the racers all behind you are SCREAMING by at top speed thanks to the rubberbanding to keep them on your tail so you just lose in the final turn. This all goes back to my 80% comment at the start - yes, you learn your lessons about some of this, but I can't help but feel like some counter-play or even a better AI balance or something could solve this. That last 20% isn't game breaking, and right up to those moments I was having fun. But a death like that can sour a good run and make me not want to do another run. That is the ultimate crime of Carmageddon, and it's why you see negative reviews - it is a Rogue-like that does NOT encourage you to just do "one more run". It takes too long to get into a good run, and you lose it in far too frustrating of a manner to encourage just one more go. But it's a shame because when you are in the thick of a good run, it is a blast to play. So take all that as you will.

Ok, I get why this has "Mixed" reviews here on Steam. If you're used to earlier installments of Carmageddon like 1, 2, or Max Damage (Or even TDR2000), this one isn't like that. This is a spinoff game that does it's own thing while still carrying the same brutal and psychotic vibes of the earlier games. I believe that Rogue Shift is a phenomenal racing game in it's own right. This game is a roguelike, I feel like the roguelike mechanics are done well, but not everyone thinks they belong in a Carmageddon game (even though this is a spinoff). A lot of the core of what makes Carmageddon is here. The gratuitous blood, gore, and violence. The rampant vehicular manslaughter. The banging soundtrack. The tight racing action to keep you on the edge of your seat. The satisfaction of turning another driver into a smoldering heap on the side of the road. It's all here. The only difference is the setting, the addition of weaponry and roguelike mechanics (which I personally love), and the fact that you're running over zombies (called "The Wasted") instead of living people (which for some people who owned a censored copy of C1 or C2, might feel familiar). To be honest though, the shambling hordes of zombies feels fitting for the Mad-Max like apocalyptic wasteland the game presents. This is one of the very few big budget arcade racing games released in the past few years, and it's actually (shockingly) very good. That in of itself is a breath of fresh air, but this game also kinda scratches that itch I've had for a good Burnout game for the past decade and a half (even then Burnout CRASH wasn't [i]good[/i]). So that's a nice bonus lol. There's even extra game modifiers that you can unlock once you finish the tournament for the first time, adding even more to the game's replay value. I'd probably wait for a sale (especially if you're still on the fence) but it's well worth buying imo.

Game is fun but it diverges considerably from what gave Carmageddon its unique and wacky charm and as a result feels a lot like other gun-up racers. Technical issues mar an otherwise engaging game loop and are the primary reason for a "no" recommendation. The Good: * Flashy graphics * Pretty environments * Satisfying physics * Primary roguelike game mode makes for interesting strategic choices * Gunplay is varied and fun * Boss encounters are challenging without being overly easy or frustrating. The Bad: * Huge stuttering issues, especially prevalent with large-scale explosives. On a high end system the game would freeze for several seconds on certain levels, particularly arenas when reaction time was an issue. * No story to speak of. * Maps are very linear. * Peds are zombies. * No wacky powerups or debuffs. * No freeform exploration. * Overly simplified and linear victory conditions Conclusion: It'd be a decent gritty racing game with better optimization and a fix for the stutter issues. Ignoring that, there's an engaging game here, but the problem is when it is compared to its namesake - this is not Carmageddon. Other than some passing references to older characters in the series, very little of Carmageddon's DNA seems to have made it into the game. As a long time fan of the series and its quirks, this bland reimagining of an old favorite doesn't live up to its legacy.
